text: This stream is sick. Nobody knows. Because nobody has ever really looked at it.
StreamChart. Every patient has a chart. Now, every stream does.
Citizen science gives a lot, and never hears back. People share an observation, nothing comes back, so they stop. And authorities can't trust data with no history and no stated confidence.
OneAquaHealth built the organs of a health system for urban streams. What was missing, was the patient.
Medicine solved this a century ago. A record that keeps the story. A level of evidence for every fact. A care loop, from symptom, to treatment, to follow-up.
So we gave every stream a medical chart.
Meet Mathis. He walks past Trois Ponts brook, which nobody has looked at for nineteen days. He takes its pulse: one photo, seven big questions, in plain words.
He answers first. Gemini looks at the same photo, but its answer is sealed, hashed the moment it arrives, until Mathis confirms his own.
Then, the reveal. They agree on the foam. They disagree on the banks. Mathis keeps his answers. The last word is always human.
And he sees, at once, what his check-up changed.
Every check-up joins the stream's chart: its state, its pulse, its whole life on one page. Every fact carries a confidence grade, from A to D.
When signs agree, the system proposes a hypothesis, never a diagnosis, with its reasons. And a care plan, quoted from the project's own catalogue of measures.
Here is a week in sixty seconds. A clearly labelled simulation, running the real engine.
Léa confirms what Mathis saw. The grade rises.
Inès reports still water. A heatwave is forecast. A seven-day health indication appears, and the stream goes into alert.
At city hall, the ward room puts it first.
The referent ecologist reviews the photos, removes a premature measure, and signs. The AI assists. A human decides.
Every citizen who contributed hears back.
Because citizen science should always answer. Your check-up triggered an inspection.
And the stream itself speaks, only with what its record contains.
For the first time in a long while, I know someone is taking care of me.
Every chart is an HL7 FHIR R4 record, accepted by a public FHIR server.
A printed sign at the foot of each stream. A school kit. No hardware.
Today, one stream in Toulouse. Tomorrow, five cities. StreamChart. They gave a medical record to a river.
